title: MATH GAOKAO - 331
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Reading a Point from a Line Graph
questions.learningObjective: Read the value of a data point from a line graph.
questions.question: A line graph shows the temperature on four days: Monday \(20^\circ\)C, Tuesday \(24^\circ\)C, Wednesday \(22^\circ\)C, and Thursday \(26^\circ\)C. What was the temperature on Wednesday?
questions.explanation: Locate Wednesday on the horizontal axis and read the corresponding value on the vertical axis. The line graph gives the Wednesday value as \(22^\circ\)C. Therefore, the temperature on Wednesday was \(22^\circ\)C.
questions.hint: Identify the point above Wednesday and read its vertical-axis value.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the total of all values shown in a line graph.
questions.question: A line graph shows monthly rainfall: January \(10\) mm, February \(15\) mm, March \(12\) mm, and April \(8\) mm. What is the total rainfall over the four months?
questions.explanation:
Add the four values shown on the line graph:
\[
10+15+12+8=45.
\]
Therefore, the total rainfall is \(45\) mm.
questions.hint: Add all the values represented by the points on the line graph.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the change in value between two consecutive points on a line graph.
questions.question: A line graph shows monthly rainfall: January \(10\) mm, February \(15\) mm, March \(12\) mm, and April \(8\) mm. What is the change from February to March?
questions.explanation:
The February value is \(15\) mm and the March value is \(12\) mm. The change is
\[
12-15=-3.
\]
A negative change means a decrease, so the rainfall decreased by \(3\) mm from February to March.
questions.hint: Subtract the earlier value from the later value and interpret the sign.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the mean of values shown in a line graph.
questions.question: A line graph shows the number of books read from Monday to Friday: Monday \(8\), Tuesday \(12\), Wednesday \(10\), Thursday \(14\), and Friday \(6\). What is the average number of books read per day?
questions.explanation:
The total number of books is
\[
8+12+10+14+6=50.
\]
There are \(5\) days, so the average is
\[
\frac{50}{5}=10.
\]
Therefore, the average number of books read per day is \(10\).
questions.hint: Find the total of all values, then divide by the number of points.

questions.concept: Rate of Change from a Line Graph
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a rate of change between two points on a line graph.
questions.question: A line graph shows distance travelled over time. At \(1\) hour, the distance is \(20\) km; at \(3\) hours, the distance is \(60\) km. What is the average speed between these two times?
questions.explanation:
The change in distance is
\[
60-20=40\text{ km}.
\]
The change in time is
\[
3-1=2\text{ h}.
\]
Thus the average speed is
\[
\frac{40}{2}=20\text{ km/h}.
\]
Therefore, the average speed is \(20\) km/h.
questions.hint: Use the change in distance divided by the change in time.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the largest decrease between consecutive points on a line graph.
questions.question: A line graph shows values for four months: January \(30\), February \(25\), March \(35\), and April \(20\). What is the largest decrease between consecutive months?
questions.explanation:
Compare consecutive changes:
\[
25-30=-5,\quad 35-25=10,\quad 20-35=-15.
\]
The decreases are \(5\) and \(15\). The largest decrease is \(15\), which occurs from March to April.
questions.hint: Find the change between each pair of consecutive points and compare the negative changes.

questions.concept: Linear Interpolation on a Line Graph
questions.learningObjective: Estimate a value between two points on a straight-line segment.
questions.question: A line graph has a straight segment joining the points \((2,10)\) and \((6,30)\). What is the value at \(x=4\)?
questions.explanation:
The segment is straight, so the value at \(x=4\) is the midpoint between \(x=2\) and \(x=6\). The average of the corresponding \(y\)-values is
\[
\frac{10+30}{2}=20.
\]
Therefore, the value at \(x=4\) is \(20\).
questions.hint: Since the segment is straight, use the midpoint between the two given points.

questions.concept: Comparing Totals from Two Line Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Compare combined totals from two line graphs in a given period.
questions.question: Two line graphs show monthly sales for Shop A and Shop B. Shop A: January \(20\), February \(30\), March \(25\). Shop B: January \(15\), February \(35\), March \(20\). In which month is the combined sales greatest?
questions.explanation:
The combined sales are:
January:
\[
20+15=35.
\]
February:
\[
30+35=65.
\]
March:
\[
25+20=45.
\]
The greatest combined sales occur in February.
questions.hint: Add the values of the two line graphs for each month, then compare.

questions.concept: Average Speed from a Distance-Time Line Graph
questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed over an interval from a distance-time line graph.
questions.question: A distance-time line graph gives the following points: at \(1\) hour, distance \(10\) km; at \(3\) hours, distance \(40\) km; at \(5\) hours, distance \(70\) km. What is the average speed from \(1\) hour to \(5\) hours?
questions.explanation:
The total distance from \(1\) hour to \(5\) hours is
\[
70-10=60\text{ km}.
\]
The total time is
\[
5-1=4\text{ h}.
\]
Thus the average speed is
\[
\frac{60}{4}=15\text{ km/h}.
\]
Therefore, the average speed is \(15\) km/h.
questions.hint: Use the overall change in distance divided by the overall change in time.

questions.concept: Missing Value from the Mean on a Line Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing point value from the mean of a line graph.
questions.question: A line graph shows values for five days: Monday \(12\), Tuesday \(15\), Wednesday \(x\), Thursday \(18\), and Friday \(20\). The mean of the five values is \(16\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
The mean is \(16\) over \(5\) days, so the total is
\[
16\times 5=80.
\]
The sum of the known values is
\[
12+15+18+20=65.
\]
Therefore,
\[
x=80-65=15.
\]
Thus the missing value is \(15\).
questions.hint: Use the mean to find the total, then subtract the known values.
